gex_data.gamma_regime: positive gamma in SPX full-chain models, but overnight SPY and futures positioning is more fragile and can amplify downside if cash SPX loses the gamma-flip area

dealer_positioning.gamma_regime: net long gamma in the dominant SPX full-chain models; near-term positioning becomes less stabilizing below roughly 7663-7685
dealer_positioning.volatility_behavior: above the gamma-flip zone dealer hedging should dampen moves; below it hedging can become pro-cyclical and expand intraday volatility
dealer_positioning.expected_behavior: 7705 is the nearest major gamma/pinning area and 7800 the dominant upside call wall; a sustained break below roughly 7663-7685 would favor faster downside and wider ranges

options_flow.skew: downside protection remains richer than upside; current short-dated 25-delta put-minus-call skew is about +1.1 to +2.3 volatility points across the near-term curve
options_flow.zero_dte_dominance: very high; recent Cboe data puts 0DTE at roughly 65-66% of total SPX options volume, making same-day gamma and strike pinning a dominant intraday influence

volatility_surface.term_structure: generally upward sloping beyond the front end; 0DTE ATM IV is about 10.3%, IV30 about 11.8%, and futures-linked ATM IV around 12.6%, while downside puts retain a positive skew premium
